essays.text: 英譯中：（15 分）During large public events, drones are increasingly used to assist securitypersonnel. Equipped with cameras, drones help officers monitor crowdmovement and respond quickly to emergencies. Supporters believe dronesimprove public safety and reduce pressure on police officers. However,some people worry about privacy and the collection of personal data.Therefore, experts believe clear regulations are needed to balance publicsafety and individual rights.
中譯英：（15 分）清明連假期間，桃園國際機場湧入大量旅客。一名安全檢查人員在行李檢查時，發現可疑物品，隨後立即通知航警，並封鎖附近相關區域。為避免引起恐慌，工作人員們冷靜引導所有旅客迅速完成通關、前往相關之登機口，並透過廣播、提供最新資訊。後來，確認該物品沒有危險，但此事件也顯示安全程序與即時應變的重要性。

英文作文：（20 分）In modern cities, public safety is not only the responsibility of the policeand security personnel. Ordinary citizens can also help prevent accidents,report suspicious activity, and provide assistance during emergencies. Inrecent years, technology and social media have changed the way peoplerespond to public safety issues. Some people believe that citizens shouldplay a more active role in helping maintain public safety, while othersthink this responsibility should primarily fall to the government and lawenforcement agencies. What is your opinion? Write a short essay ofapproximately 250 words to explain your views and provide details orexamples to support your answer.代號： 50160-50660頁次： 5－2

Consequently, energy prices have surged, raising both manufacturing and raw material costs. Experts also warn that 30 oil prices remain elevated for several months, companies will eventually pass these higher costs on to consumers.

mcq.q: What is the primary argument of the passage?
opts: Global cooperation has completely replaced competition.
Strategic competition is redefining international relations.
Military conflict is the dominant form of rivalry.
Economic globalization is no longer relevant.
mcq.passage: In recent years, the global order has undergone a gradual but significant transformation, marked by a shift from cooperative interdependence toward strategic competition among major powers. Rather than engaging in direct confrontation, countries increasingly deploy indirect instruments—such as economic sanctions, technological restrictions, and selective alliances—to consolidate influence while minimizing overt conflict. This shift in geopolitical dynamics reflects a deeper reconfiguration of globalization itself. Economic interdependence, once regarded as a stabilizing mechanism that reduced the likelihood of conflict, is now perceived as a potential vulnerability. Countries have begun to reassess their reliance on global supply chains, particularly in sectors deemed critical to national security. Consequently, policies that emphasize resilience and self-sufficiency have gained prominence, even at the cost of economic efficiency. At the same time, technological leadership has emerged as a defining dimension of geopolitical rivalry. Control over advanced technologies—especially in artificial intelligence and semiconductor production—is no longer merely an economic objective but a strategic imperative. This development has intensified competition while also raising barriers to international collaboration. Although such strategies may yield short-term advantages, they risk accelerating the fragmentation of the global system into competing blocs. In the long run, this fragmentation may undermine collective efforts to address transnational challenges. Thus, the evolving geopolitical landscape reflects not only intensified competition but also a growing tension between national security and global cooperation.

mcq.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
opts: AI is significantly enhancing cybersecurity defenses against all threats.
Cybercrime is declining due to technological progress.
AI is transforming cybercrime into a more advanced threat.
Traditional scams are becoming less common.
mcq.passage: According to recent reports, 2026 is widely regarded as one of the most perilous years for internet users, as cybercrime continues to evolve through the use of artificial intelligence. Researchers note that AI tools are no longer limited to routine automation but are now used to enhance cyberattack techniques such as phishing and social engineering. By combining large language models with deepfake technologies, attackers can convincingly impersonate trusted individuals, making scams more difficult to detect and resist. One particularly concerning trend is the rise of highly personalized scams, including so-called“pig butchering” schemes. These schemes involve criminals building emotional relationships with targets over extended periods before introducing fraudulent investment opportunities. With AI, such operations can be carried out at scale while maintaining a high degree of personalization, blurring the line between automated and human interaction. Cybersecurity experts also warn of a potentially more disruptive phase in AI-driven risks. A leaked blog post from Anthropic described its upcoming model, Mythos, as a possible“watershed moment”with serious security implications. The model is believed to have the ability to identify and exploit system vulnerabilities at unprecedented speed, raising concerns about large-scale cyberattacks if such technologies are realized. Advances in autonomous malware add further risk. Some AI-driven systems can modify their own code during execution, allowing them to evade detection and adapt to defensive measures. Experts stress that these developments not only increase the scale of cybercrime but also make it more sophisticated and unpredictable. Although AI can strengthen cybersecurity defenses, experts highlight a key imbalance: attackers need only find one vulnerability, while defenders must secure entire systems. This suggests that digital security will become increasingly complex and difficult to manage.

They reduce the need for direct human interaction.
They operate primarily within financial institutions.
